subtopic: A power cut or rain spoils plans
subtype: Approach: making a back-up plan for outdoor events [Thinking]
passage: Monday. Aditi's birthday was planned for the garden on Saturday. Her friend Imran pushed his glasses up and said the clouds looked heavy. "Then we need a Plan B," Aditi said. "If it rains we move to the hall behind the flats. Two sets of games: cards and skipping ropes for outside, board games and pass-the-parcel for inside." She packed two boxes. Saturday. Rain began at three. Everyone carried cake, chairs and the inside box into the hall within five minutes. Sunday. Imran said, "That was the best birthday I have been to, even with the rain." Aditi grinned and put both boxes back on the shelf, ready for next time.

qa.q: What did Aditi pack in the two boxes?
qa.a: She packed cards and skipping ropes for outside, and board games and pass-the-parcel for inside.

qa.q: What was Aditi feeling when Imran said the clouds looked heavy?
qa.a: A little worried that rain might spoil the party, but ready, since she made a Plan B on the spot.

qa.q: What else could Aditi add to her plan for the birthday?
qa.a: She could tell the guests about the hall option in advance, so everyone knows where to go if the weather changes.

qa.q: How did Imran see the birthday when the rain came?
qa.a: As the best birthday he had been to, because the move was quick and the party carried on.

grounding: A girl planning a garden birthday makes a rain plan with the hall and keeps games ready for both places.
